question:
I am defining a dbt model configuration to create a set of tables that have a number of common columns. Currently the YAML file looks like this:

version: 2

models:
  - name: table1
    columns:
      - name: id
        description: The identifier
      - name: attribute1
        description: Attribute 1
  - name: table2
    columns:
      - name: id
        description: The identifier
      - name: attribute2
        description: Attribute 2

I would like this to be more DRY, so I tried using the <<: merge operator which works somehow but it does not retain the information about the column descriptions for some reason:

version: 2

.comm: &comm
  columns:
    - name: id
      description: The identifier

models:
  - name: table1
    <<: *comm
    columns:
      - name: attribute1
        description: Attribute 1
  - name: table2
    <<: *comm
    columns:
      - name: attribute2
        description: Attribute 2

Am I missing something? Are there other options to avoid repeating the same set of columns in the YAML file defining a dbt model configuration?

Edit: the set of common columns would be quite large and each column would have its own description, data type and tests.
title: Reuse columns in dbt model
answer: Your concern may be similar https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/issues/1790 that is not yet supported by dbt.
